experiment.name: POST_LOAD_LDD_RESOLUTION_DIVERGENCE
experiment.scope: disposable local process; no production/canonical state mutation
experiment.intervention: Load SQLite normally, then change LD_LIBRARY_PATH to an alternate temporary libsqlite3.so.0 location and invoke ldd on the already imported _sqlite3 extension.

observed.proc_self_maps: remained bound to the libsqlite3 object already mapped before the environment change
observed.ldd: resolved the alternate temporary libsqlite3.so.0 for a new loader-resolution observation

grf_collapse.generated_reality: Running ldd on the _sqlite3 extension after SQLite is loaded is sufficient evidence for the exact libsqlite3 object active in the observing process.
grf_collapse.counter_reality: ldd performs dependency resolution for a fresh loader invocation and can diverge from the object already mapped into the live process.
grf_collapse.falsifier: Post-load LD_LIBRARY_PATH divergence while comparing ldd resolution against /proc/self/maps.
grf_collapse.architecture_consequence: Do not use ldd as admission truth for the active SQLite object. Prefer /proc/self/maps device+inode+path, O_NOFOLLOW open, fstat device/inode equality and hashing of the opened backing object; retain ldd as diagnostic-only evidence.

fusion.relationship: Mapped-object attestation and release-accepted identity are separate invariants. The merged V5 identity fence does not prove which bytes the production service mapped; the mapped-object discriminator does not by itself prove those bytes are release-safe. Both must compose with deployment-owned runtime and root-anchor/service-start evidence.

remaining_counterevidence_and_blockers: The accepted productive path previously observed SQLite 3.45.1-1ubuntu2.7 and no production root anchor.
The fixed runtime is not yet proven installed and deployment-owned on the actual Frank service path.
Service start/restart/rollback, downgrade/library-swap and parent loader-environment continuity remain production gates.
Semantic-lineage selection and recovery obligations in F-V01-13 remain independent and open.
